messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging on-call: high error rate + KV cache growth observed in continuous-batching pool 'cb-prod-us-west' — auto-escalating to S1. Logs show repeated cache insert storms and token batching spikes. Monitor: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/CB_Pool
Sarah L.: on it. seeing lots of 502s and OOMs on rtx-pool-3. Are we sure this is continuous batching config related?
Pradeep: yup — traces show huge batch sizes (num_seqs=64, batch_tokens>120k) causing cache churn. Looks like a bad rollout of a new routing policy with max_batch_tokens accidentally set to very high value.
Danny: confirmed: recent rollout 1717999000 updated default route config and increased max_batch_tokens from 8192 -> 131072 for throughput testing. That interacts badly with max_num_seqs defaults.
Marta: customer impact — API error rate spiked ~18% over last 10m, p50 latency up 2x. A handful of high-volume tenants hit retriable 502s, some timeouts. Support ticket queue is filling.
Sarah L.: immediate mitigation plan: 1) disable continuous batching on cb-prod-us-west as a blunt stop; 2) roll back the route config to previous max_batch_tokens; 3) scale down kv_cache TTLs or evict large entries. Will do 1) now.
Danny: +1. How to disable quickly?
Pradeep: route-level override exists. Run:
```
rbctl routes set cb-prod-us-west --continuous-batching=false --reason "incident: cache blowup"
```
This avoids an infra restart.
Sarah L.: executing rbctl now...
Sarah L.: done. response: ok. continuous-batching disabled for cb-prod-us-west.
incident-bot: action logged: route override applied by Sarah L.
Carter: I'm seeing CPU drop and fewer OOM kills already. Error rate falling but some batch workers still have high mem.
Danny: next rollback: revert the bad config that bumped max_batch_tokens. Pradeep can you patch the config in git and trigger canary?
Pradeep: pushing config rollback and doing a targeted canary for non-prod then prod. Patch:
```
max_batch_tokens: 8192
max_num_seqs: 8
batch_timeout_ms: 30
```
Applying to route defaults.
Marta: support update: telling affected customers (acct ids: acct_834, acct_1127) that we have mitigation in place and are investigating. Opening incident page for external status.
Sarah L.: after disabling continuous batching, we still saw a KV cache size metric sticky at high values. Will trigger manual KV cache eviction on the affected nodes: `curl -XPOST http://node-api/kv_cache/evict?pool=cb-prod-us-west&threshold=0.8`
Danny: be careful — evict can cause short latency spike while caches repopulate. Proceed when you're ready.
Sarah L.: doing evict now.
Sarah L.: evict returned success, cache size trending down. Error rate back near baseline (5% -> 1.2%). Latency p95 better but not fully recovered.
Pradeep: note — continuous batching re-enabled later must use conservative defaults. Propose changing global defaults and adding guardrail: max_batch_tokens <= 16384 for hosted routes, max_num_seqs <= 16, backpressure timeouts. Also add a validation step in route rollout to reject batch sizes above threshold unless explicit opt-in.
Marta: filing incident ticket INC-2026-041 with impact summary and next steps for communication and RCA.
Support Bot: Created INC-2026-041; notified support on-call and created draft status page entry.
Danny: follow-ups: (a) add a runbook entry for continuous-batching regressions (how to disable route, evict kv cache, revert config), (b) add metric alert for batch_tokens spike and KV_CACHE_growth alert threshold, (c) consider hard-limiting batch tokens at runtime to prevent config accidents.
Sarah L.: handing over to Marta for the remainder of the on-call window. I'm going offline in 30m. Marta, I'll drop notes in the incident doc.
Marta: taking over. Thanks Sarah. Quick notes: we should monitor slow-recovery customers and consider targeted resends for in-flight requests if needed. Also check Dedicated pools for any spillover.
Carter: one last datapoint — we saw 3 replica restarts due to OOM from the wolfpack of large batches. Kernel OOM logs attached in thread. Will retain pod logs for postmortem.
Pradeep: immediate config hotfix pushed to prod canary; will watch for any other pools with similar rollout flags.
Marta: for post-incident: prioritize adding a safety check in the config API that rejects accidental 10x increases to max_batch_tokens without an explicit "danger" flag and an approval flow. Also add a short-term mitigation: if kv_cache growth rate > 2x baseline, autoscale down continuous-batching workers or pause batching automatically.
Support Bot: Support alerted customers via email template "CB_INCIDENT_2026_041".
Marta: lowering priority to monitoring / RCA tasks. If anyone sees a late spike, re-ping on this thread. Thanks all.
Sarah L.: noted. Good recovery.
incident-bot: incident INC-2026-041 marked as mitigated at 1718000305 by Marta. Postmortem assigned to Pradeep + Danny.
Marta: I'll take the handoff to create the postmortem doc and schedule a 30m RCA tomorrow. Will include config diff, timeline, and action items (runbook, API guardrail, alert thresholds).
Danny: adding test to CI that simulates large sequence workloads to ensure KV cache stabilizes under new defaults.
Pradeep: also will add a quick dashboard showing "batch_tokens per request" distribution to spot future regressions earlier.
Marta: thanks team — closing active mitigation. Follow-ups tracked in INC-2026-041/postmortem.
